analyst_view.overall: Gent (18th) and Red Star (15th) both have 4 points, so this goes a long way to deciding which of them stays in the race for the play-off places; Rik De Mil said it is not yet a must-win game but Gent must be solid at home. Gent's injury list grew on Wednesday: playmaker Laszlo Benes is out with a foot problem, on top of Tibe De Vlieger (hamstring), Michel-Ange Balikwisha and Pieter Gerkens, none of whom the numbers know about. Red Star travel with 21 players but without the suspended Aleksandar Katai (counted), top scorer Bamba Dieng (back) and Timi Max Elsnik; Marko Arnautovic is back in the squad after illness but how long he can play is unclear, and Stefan Gudelj returns from suspension. Coach Albert Riera wants a calm, controlled game that is 'dull' for Gent and said he worries more about conceding than scoring; no referee is named in the brief.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals (1.8 Gent, 0.8 Red Star). I lean lower, to about 2.4: Gent now also lose Benes, their main creator, alongside Balikwisha, Gerkens and De Vlieger, and Red Star are without top scorer Dieng and Elsnik with Arnautovic only just over an illness, none of which is on the numbers' list. Riera's plan for a slow, controlled game points the same way; Katai's ban is already counted.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, mostly Gent's, already nudged up for both sides' recent corner counts. Without Balikwisha and Benes Gent have less wide play and lose a set-piece taker, but a Red Star side that sits back and controls transitions tends to concede corners to the home side, so nothing clearly moves the total and I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Gent's quiet recent record (-8%) and Red Star's higher count (+3%) already in. The stakes are real for both and Gudelj, a combative midfielder, is back from a ban, but no referee is named and nothing the numbers miss clearly points either way, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots. I lean a little lower, to about 25.3, because Gent's injury list takes out several creators including Benes, Red Star travel without a fit first-choice striker, and Riera wants a calm game that gives Gent little. Gent's recent dip (-9%) and Red Star's busy shooting (+9.5%) are already counted, so the size stays small.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target, already cut for Gent hitting the target far less than expected lately (-14%). With Benes, Balikwisha, Gerkens and De Vlieger out for Gent and Dieng missing for Red Star, I lean a little lower: -6% gives about 8.2.
